title: 17 Money Lessons: Iman Gadzhi on opportunity cost, cash flow, and investing in yourself
summary: Iman Gadzhi talks to his younger self about money mistakes: inaction and comfort cost more than any purchase, cash flow beats revenue, and early income should be reinvested in yourself and tools. He also covers lifestyle creep, geographic arbitrage, buying used, and why passive income is not passive.

principles.text: Opportunity cost, the businesses and side hustles you never start, is the biggest expense in your life.
principles.quote: the biggest expense in your life will be opportunity cost.

principles.text: Focus on cash flow and profit first; revenue is vanity. Chase enterprise value only later.
principles.quote: revenue is vanity, profit is sanity, and cash flow is reality.

principles.text: Treat tools and software as investments that stack competitive advantages, even as a solopreneur.
principles.quote: investing in your business tools isn't a cost it is an investment to have a competitive advantage

principles.text: Early income should be reinvested in yourself, since you are the company's whole output.
principles.quote: when you're making your first few thousands and your first few tens of thousands, that should all be reinvested in yourself

principles.text: Don't let lifestyle creep follow income; save and invest most of what you earn early on.
principles.quote: if I doubled my income, I didn't all of a sudden double my expenses.

principles.text: Wealthy people ask how much a purchase will lose, not what it costs; buy used and let others eat depreciation.
principles.quote: Truly wealthy people do do not ask how much does it cost. They ask how much will I lose?
